Subject: MAP: Performance evaluation & quantization audit — Nimbus Labs

Hi Jake / Emily,

Attaching the latest Mutual Action Plan (v1.3) and the baseline performance plan we discussed on the call. The objective for this MAP is to get Nimbus to GA on Redwood Dedicated by the end of Q2 while validating performance at target concurrency for your typical 512-token sequences. Key asks in this phase:

- Run MAP perf sweep across FP16/BF16 (baseline) and INT8/INT4 (quant variants) for the two critical models: large-chat-v2 and embed-compact-v1.
- Capture TTFT (time-to-first-token), p95 token latency, and end-to-end throughput at concurrencies of 8, 32, 128.
- Produce kernel profiles (per-layer op breakdown) and highlight any INT8 regressed kernels.

Deliverables and timeline (high level) are in the attached PDF — proposed close timeline is: perf sign-off by 2027-04-20, procurement/PO by 2027-05-05, and Dedicated start week of 2027-05-10.

Attachments: nimbus_map_v1.3.pdf, perf_quant_profiles_Q8_Q4.csv

Can you confirm we have access to the test cluster we used in POC and whether your security team needs any additional attestations before we share kernel traces?

Thanks,
Rafael

Rafael / Neha,

Thanks — received the MAP and the perf plan. A couple of quick clarifications before we start runs next week:

1) Test cluster: we can reprovision the POC cluster for you, but procurement requires a minimal data processing agreement before we exchange kernel traces. Is a short NDA addendum sufficient?
2) Sequence lengths: our 75% percentile is 420 tokens, 95% is 860 — can you add an 860 token bucket to the sweep for the large-chat-v2 model?
3) Target metrics: can you confirm p95 latency SLO target for INT8 at concurrency 32? We want to understand acceptable regression vs FP16.

Also attaching a short logfile from our POC runs where we observed an unexpected tail spike on p99 in INT8 — filename: kernel_trace_int8_vs_fp16.zip (small).

—Jake

Jake — appreciate the log. Short answers inline:

1) NDA addendum: yes, that'll be fine. Priyom will send the standard kernel-trace addendum and a checklist for what we need redacted.
2) Added: we will include an 860-token sweep for large-chat-v2. That will target TTFT, p95, p99, and end-to-end throughput.
3) p95 SLO for INT8 at concurrency 32: proposed SLO is <= 220 ms per token p95 for tokens after the first stream (TTFT excluded). For FP16 baseline we expect p95 ~ 160 ms in the same run. If INT8 exceeds 20% regression vs FP16 at p95, it flags for a kernel regression deep-dive.

Next steps:
- Priyom to share the kernel-trace NDA and the perf-run checklist (EOD today).
- Nimbus to provision test cluster and kick sweep by 2027-04-14.
- We will consolidate results by 2027-04-18 for an internal QA pass and share a short summary with you (CSV + annotated kernel profiles).

Neha

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance evaluation & quantization audit — Nimbus Labs

Jake / Emily — thank you and the Nimbus eng team for completing the sweep. Summary of the deliverables we just uploaded to the shared Drive and the quick findings:

- Deliverables: perf_quant_profiles_Q8_Q4.csv (aggregated metrics), nimbus_map_v1.3.pdf (updated MAP with close dates), kernel_profiles_summary.pdf (annotated per-layer notes)
- Key findings (short):
  - FP16 baseline: p95 token latency (concurrency 32, 512 tokens) = 158 ms; TTFT = 120 ms; throughput = 14.8k tokens/sec sustained
  - INT8: p95 (same bucket) = 198 ms (25% regression vs FP16) — exceeds our 20% threshold and flagged for kernel deep-dive
  - INT4 (experimental): produced higher memory savings but widespread quality instability on large-chat-v2; recommending experimental label for production MAP
  - 860-token bucket: INT8 p99 showed occasional tail spikes correlated to a specific attention-kernel (layer 23) — we attached the kernel trace for that layer.

Action items and next steps:
- Redwood (Neha & Priyom): deep-dive on layer-23 INT8 kernel; propose two mitigations (kernel fallback to FP16 for that layer, or per-layer retrain-aware quant calibration) by 2027-04-21.
- Nimbus: confirm whether procurement can accept the MAP as-is pending perf remediations (PO target 2027-05-05).
- Joint review scheduled: 2027-04-21T10:00-10:45 PT (we will share dial-in).

If Nimbus wants a quick patch to avoid the INT8 tail in the interim, we can offer a conservative production profile that pins layer 23 to FP16 while quantizing the rest — we can ship that as a config toggle within 48 hours. Please confirm.

Thanks,
Rafael
